## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

These are tones of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the \`plot()' function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-built data frame `cars` to play with plotting: 

```{r}
cars
```
```{r}
head(cars)
```
```{r}
plot(cars)
```
Now with ggplot: 
> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot")` in my quarto document as this will result in me re-installing the package every time I render my report. 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the input data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (the way you want the plot drawn, like points, lines, columns)

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ggsci)
theme_nature <- function(base_size = 7, base_family = "Arial") {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) +
    theme(
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.25),
      axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.25),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
      legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"),
      strip.background = element_blank()
    )
}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method= "lm", se=TRUE, color = "blue") + 
  theme_nature() + 
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)", 
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)", 
       title = "The Long Drive")
```
### Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from online:

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
nrow(genes)
ncol(genes)
table(genes$State)
library(viridis)
GLP1plot <- ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(Condition1, Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("orange","purple","red") ) +
  labs(x="Control (no drug)", 
       y="Drug Treated",
       title = "Gene expression changes upon drug treatment", 
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo") 
GLP1plot
```

!= is the not equals function
```{r}
sum(genes$State == "up")
```

> Q. What percentage of genes are "down" regulated? 

```{r}
down_genes <-  sum(genes$State == "down")
total_genes <- sum(nrow(genes))
down_genes/total_genes

ans <- round(down_genes/total_genes * 100,4)
ans
```
##I could've also done n.total <- nrow(genes)

The percentage of down genes is `r ans` % 

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 ) /
      (p3 | p4)
```
```{r}
GLP1plot + 
  facet_wrap(~State)
```

### The Gap Minder

The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lots of stuff to plot. 
```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)

head(gapminder)

```

> Q. How many data entires are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```


> Q. How many countries are in this dataset? 

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, gdpPercap, col = continent) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth() 
  
```
Histograms of 

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill= continent) + 
  geom_histogram()
```
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent) + 
  geom_boxplot()
```
